claims.exact_statement: For a background-subtracted excess field b(x) in a steady front frame satisfying D b'' + v_rel b' - k b = 0 on a source-free tail, with constant D>0, v_rel>0, k>=0, the decaying exponential length is ell=2D/(v_rel+sqrt(v_rel^2+4Dk)); hence ell<=D/v_rel and a requested passive length ell_target is feasible only if v_rel*ell_target<=D.
assumptions: The field is linear and scalar in the tail.
Diffusivity and clearance are constant in space/time and D is the effective lateral diffusivity in the material-cell frame.
The front-relative cell-row speed v_rel is known and positive.
There is no distributed source, positive local amplification, nonlinear saturation, or contact-dependent transport in the fitted tail.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_exact_conditional_model_lemma; equation is standard moving-frame transport mathematics, not a theorem about tissue
claims.novelty_boundary: No novelty claim for the advection-diffusion calculation. Candidate contribution is its falsifiable application as a reach-speed design boundary for the 2026 Drosophila surface-Fog/mechanical wave; the biological interface is unvalidated.

costs.inputs_supplied_in_this_audit: Cross-paper reported means and profile lengths only.
inputs_not_yet_acquired: same-condition front speed relative to cell rows
surface-associated Fog mobility in that same material frame
first-order active-pool clearance under a matched perturbation
costs.runtime: constant-time evaluation after parameters are measured
costs.experimental_resources: custom reporters/perturbation genotypes, embryo-level live imaging and FCS/pulse-chase; quantitative labor/energy costs not estimated

claims.falsifier: A same-condition background-subtracted passive tail with measured k>=0 but v_rel*ell>D, or systematic failure of predicted ell across held-out doses after uncertainty accounting, falsifies this reduced model.
claims.next_gate: Measure D, k, v_rel, and ell in the same Fog-dose/Gprk2/integrin perturbation series and compare held-out profiles with the no-transport cell-local model.

claims.exact_statement: Using the 2019 reported wave-speed mean 2.2 um/min as a provisional proxy for v_rel and the 2026 FCS means D_slow=1.6 um^2/s and D_fast=55 um^2/s, the zero-clearance lengths D/v are approximately 43.6 um and 1500 um, respectively; across 70 um, estimated Peclet numbers vL/D are 1.60 and 0.047.
assumptions: Cross-paper speed is an acceptable proxy for material-row speed for dimensional screening only.
The measured slow FCS component is a surface-associated mobile pool with effective lateral D_slow.
70 um is used as the spatial comparison span of the 2026 surface-pool profile.
claims.novelty_boundary: Dimensional consistency is not evidence of causality, fit, or priority. Cross-paper numbers are not paired observations.

costs.input_data: Source-reported means; reported plus/minus terms are treated only as corner intervals, not confidence intervals.
costs.computation: Python 3 scalar arithmetic; no tissue simulation, fitting, or raw-data analysis.

claims.falsifier: Matched same-condition D_slow and v_rel produce a materially different scale, or Fogslow is not a mobile surface-associated pool.
claims.next_gate: Repeat the calculation on paired, embryo-level mobility and cell-relative speed estimates with propagated measurement uncertainty.

claims.exact_statement: A single spatial profile P(x) observed under a monotone front can be reproduced by a no-transport cell-age waveform M(a)=P(v_rel*a); in particular, an exponential local waveform produces the same exponential profile with ell=v_rel*tau. Therefore a spatial snapshot alone does not identify moving surface-pool transport.
assumptions: A front maps distance into a response coordinate s=x/v_rel.
A per-cell response waveform has an exponential segment over the measured window.
The currently cited data do not measure same-condition cell trajectories and bound-pool clearance sufficiently to exclude this alternative.
claims.status: constructed_adversarial_model_alias; non-identifiability for the present observations, not a claim that cells use this exact waveform
claims.novelty_boundary: The space-time coordinate identity is elementary. Its purpose is to prevent interpreting a front-frame profile as proof of lateral ligand transport.

costs.required_measurements: cell-linked MyoII time course, first vitelline-contact time, cell-row-relative front speed, surface-Fog mobility/clearance, and embryo-level profile
costs.runtime: profile reconstruction and held-out error comparison after data acquisition

claims.falsifier: The alternative is rejected only if the measured per-cell waveform fails to predict spatial profiles across perturbations while the transport model predicts held-out conditions.
claims.next_gate: Fit both reduced models to a subset of perturbations; hold out one Fog/Gprk2 dose and one integrin condition.

claims.exact_statement: In the reported 2026 experimental conditions, primordium-only G-alpha restoration and source-confined membrane-tethered Fog do not sustain WT-like MyoII wave propagation, and increasing Fog/Gprk2 signaling range is reported to slow the invagination wave; the complete relay therefore includes propagation-zone GPCR/Fog and adhesion/de-adhesion effects.
assumptions: The source-reported genetic constructs, embryo staging, and measured row-count/speed assays are valid for their stated Drosophila context.
The claim is limited to reported perturbation conditions and does not generalize across tissues/species.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is the source study's reported mechanism and a pre-existing mechanical-relay baseline, not our discovery.

costs.source_reported: Genetic perturbations, embryo-level imaging/FCS, cell tracking; exact experimental cost not estimated.
costs.audit: No raw image data or external supplementary datasets reanalyzed.

claims.falsifier: A replicated, matched condition showing WT-like propagation without propagation-zone Fog/GPCR or without Fog dispersal would falsify the stated necessity within that condition.
claims.next_gate: Use the published rescue/tethered controls as matched-initiation baselines in any predictive dose-series experiment.

claims.exact_statement: A calibrated mapping from Fog-source dose, Gprk2-mediated surface clearance, integrin-dependent contact/cofactor activity, and front speed to a target contractility footprint could support engineering a tissue-wave reach/speed frontier; no such controller or mapping has been validated in this work.
assumptions: Surface-pool D and k can be separately measured and manipulated.
Cell-relative speed and contact geometry are observable and reproducible.
The reduced model or a fitted contact-age alternative predicts held-out perturbations.
Safety/viability and whole-embryo outcomes are included in the objective before any real-world application.
claims.novelty_boundary: The source papers already establish mechanogen gradients and adhesion-dependent wave speed. The new candidate is the quantitatively parameterized, held-out reach-speed design interface; novelty/priority is not established.

parameter_acquisition: FCS or pulse-chase/FRAP for surface-pool mobility and clearance
live confocal tracking of cell rows/contact/detachment and MyoII/βPS reporters
Fog-source and Gprk2 dose series with integrin factorial control
embryo-level replication, genotype construction, microscopy time

claims.falsifier: The reduced design law fails if it cannot predict held-out profile/speed data or the cell-local kinetic model is equally predictive after equal parameter acquisition.
claims.next_gate: Acquire paired same-condition data, then decide whether to retain, extend with integrin gain, or reject the passive range-speed law.

failures_and_unknowns.statement: MyoII decay length is not established to equal Fogslow transport length; direct inversion into k is not a biological rate measurement.
Slow FCS Fog is only presumed membrane-associated/receptor-bound, and the molecular integrin-GPCR coupling is explicitly unresolved by the 2026 source.
2026 speed, FCS diffusivity, MyoII lengths and Fogslow profiles are not supplied here as a matched same-embryo parameter set; a 2019 speed proxy was used only for scale screening.

Classic morphogen literature already models diffusion, receptor binding, endocytosis/internalization, and ligand degradation; no novelty claim is supported for a multi-pool reaction-transport model or clearance-controlled length scale.
No wound-healing, regeneration, cross-species intervention, or whole-organism safety outcome was tested. Hydra mechanical organizer steering is cited as prior art, not an outcome of this work.
